about.title: Martinez Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Martinez sits at the crossroads of Contra Costa County's industrial and shipping activity, from refinery-adjacent facilities to warehouses and job sites off I-680 and SR-4. Workers here face real risks: heavy equipment, vehicle traffic on busy corridors like Alhambra Avenue, and physically demanding tasks that lead to falls, strains, and worse. California generally requires injured workers to go through workers' compensation rather than sue their employer directly, but that's not the whole story. When a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver contributed to your injury, a separate third-party claim may be available alongside your comp benefits. LawProactive doesn't practice law or charge fees to connect you. We simply help Martinez workers find an independent attorney who can sort out which paths apply to their situation and pursue every available option on a contingency basis, meaning no fee unless there's a recovery.

items.question: I was hurt at a job site off SR-4 near Martinez. Can I sue my employer directly?
items.answer: In most cases, California workers' compensation is the exclusive remedy against your employer, regardless of who was at fault. However, if another company, such as a subcontractor or equipment supplier, contributed to the accident, you may have a separate third-party claim. An independent attorney can review the details of your job site to determine what applies.

items.question: What if my employer retaliates after I report an injury?
items.answer: Retaliation for reporting a workplace injury is illegal under California law. If you experience reduced hours, demotion, or termination after reporting, an attorney can advise you on your options separate from your workers' comp claim.

items.question: How long do I have to report my injury or file a claim?
items.answer: You generally need to notify your employer within 30 days of a workplace injury to preserve your workers' comp benefits. If a third party contributed to your injury, that separate claim typically carries a two-year deadline. Because these timelines run differently, it helps to get guidance early.
